summary: Reserve buffer credits reclassified as usage_adjustment after out-of-order hourly postbacks
description:
Issue summary:
BrightPath Health reported that their latest finalized invoice (2026-03-01 to 2026-03-07) contains a new line item 'usage_adjustment' equal to the value of previously expected 'reserve_buffer' credits. They assert that reserved buffer credits (hourly free buffer for enterprise plan) were converted to usage_adjustment after a retroactive reclassification and resulted in a $4,120 unexpected net charge.

Impact:
- Customer-facing invoice shows unexpected charge affecting month-end close for BrightPath Finance team.
- Customer's applications were unaffected functionally; this is a billing attribution/regression.

Timeline (customer-provided):
- 2026-03-07 01:03 UTC: hourly postbacks arrived late for several micro-batches.
- 2026-03-07 03:12 UTC: BrightPath noticed provisional invoice change in console.
- 2026-03-09 10:20 UTC: Customer opened support ticket via in-product chat.

Steps to reproduce (high level):
1) Run multi-tenant batch embedding job across 3 regions with reserved buffer tags enabled.
2) Simulate delayed postback ingestion (network partition) so some hourly postbacks are processed out-of-order.
3) Finalized invoice shows reserve_buffer credits missing and a compensating usage_adjustment line.

Attachments/Logs provided by customer:
- invoice_pdf_2026-03-07.pdf
- postback_samples.json (subset of late postbacks)
- support_chat_transcript_2026-03-09.txt

Notes: customer requests provisional credit while we investigate and a clear explanation of why reserve buffer credits were reclassified rather than preserved.
comments: 2026-03-09 - Maya Chen (Support): Received initial report from BrightPath. Logged billing ticket and requested latest invoice PDF and sample postbacks. Escalating to Billing Eng and Postback team.

2026-03-09 - Omar Singh (Billing Eng): Acknowledged. Pulling billing events and postback ingestion timeline for BrightPath's org_id=org_brightpath_42. Will check hourly-accumulator audit logs and finalization pass.

2026-03-10 - Elena Rodriguez (Postback Team): Found a short window where the postback-reconciler replay logic applied late postbacks into a retroactive reconciliation pass (PR #289). Suspecting a bug where 'reserve_buffer' tag TTL expired before reclassification, causing credit to be applied as usage_adjustment. Collecting message offsets from kafka-topic postbacks-us-east-1.

2026-03-11 - BrightPath Finance (Customer): Requesting provisional credit ASAP. Concerned this will impact their internal chargebacks. Asked for timeline for fix and whether invoices will be reissued.

2026-03-12 - Omar Singh (Billing Eng): Confirmed provisional credit pathway and created a hold to prevent autopay for affected invoice until resolution. Notified Finance ops to schedule a temporary credit in ledger while engineers complete fix.

2026-03-12 - Support (Maya Chen): Notified BrightPath that we placed an invoice hold and initiated provisional credit. Asked for permission to re-run reconciliation once the postback ordering fix is deployed. Customer granted permission.

2026-03-12 - Elena Rodriguez (Postback Team): Deployed hotfix to postback-reconciler to guard against TTL expiry when applying reserve_buffer tags in retroactive passes. Will run end-to-end replay in staging and then a controlled reprocessing for customer's window in prod.
investigation_notes: Queried billing_events table for org_brightpath_42 between 2026-03-06 and 2026-03-08. Found 37 late postbacks with ingestion_timestamp > event_timestamp by 1.5-2.5 hours.
Hourly accumulator showed buffer_token_usage decreased to 0 for the affected hourly buckets before finalization job ran at 2026-03-07T04:00:00Z.

Postback-reconciler PR #289 introduced an optimization that allows retroactive application of postbacks but had an edge condition: reserve_buffer tag TTL (24h) was being checked against wall-clock rather than event-time during replays, causing expired-tag logic to trigger and reclassify credit as usage_adjustment.

Kafka offsets for topic postbacks-us-east-1: low=1234567 high=1234689. Late postbacks fall in offsets 1234590-1234626. Collected sample messages and validated presence of reserve_buffer tag in payload.
Billing rerun simulation in staging reproduced credit reclassification when TTL check used wall-clock. When using event-time TTL, credits preserved correctly.
No other customers observed in a quick scan of 1000 random orgs; limited to multi-region batch jobs with delayed postbacks near hourly-finalization boundaries.
Risk assessment: medium. Causes incorrect charges but not data loss. Affects enterprise customers running cross-region bulk jobs.
resolution: Workaround: placed invoice hold and issued provisional ledger credit for $4,120 pending reprocessing. Technical fix: rolled back TTL wall-clock check and shipped hotfix to postback-reconciler to use event-time TTL for reserve_buffer tag checks (deployed 2026-03-12 18:40 UTC). Next steps: controlled reprocessing of affected hourly buckets for org_brightpath_42 to reapply reserve_buffer credits correctly and regenerate final invoice lines. Finance to confirm ledger adjustments and reissue corrected invoice if required. Follow-ups: postmortem on 2026-03-16, add unit test to postback-reconciler for TTL behavior, and update runbook 'Postback Ordering Runbook' to include this edge case.
